description: pkg_a/run.py#main and pkg_b/cli.py#main are unrelated functions in different packages that happen to share a bare name. tests/test_cli.py imports only pkg_b's main. A test file that imports a same-named symbol from an unrelated module must not be reported as an import_relationship candidate for pkg_a's main: that import asserts no relationship to pkg_a/run.py at all, so it is at most a naming_heuristic. Regression case for ORB-12411.

unchanged_symbols.note: The other package's `main`, byte-identical across the change. Sharing a bare name with pkg_a's `main` must not, by itself, attach tests/test_cli.py to pkg_a's `main` as an import_relationship.

candidate_tests.rationale: tests/test_cli.py imports `pkg_b.cli.main`. Its bare name matches pkg_a/run.py's `main`, but the import specifier names a different module, so this is a name-only association, not an observed import edge to pkg_a's `main`.
